title: FDA Endpoints and Noninferiority Margins for Antibacterial Approvals in cUTI and CABP
summary: The primary endpoints, analysis populations and noninferiority margins FDA has accepted in cUTI and CABP antibacterial approvals, from guidance defaults to recent precedent.
body_markdown:
## FDA endpoints and noninferiority margins for antibacterial approvals in cUTI and CABP


FDA's accepted efficacy standards for complicated urinary tract infection (cUTI) and community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) differ in structure. For cUTI, FDA recommends a composite of clinical and microbiological response in a microbiologically defined population, with a 10-percentage-point noninferiority (NI) margin[59](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=59)[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=60) . For CABP, it recommends an early, symptom-based clinical response endpoint with a 12.5-percentage-point margin[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=70)[72](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=72) . Approvals since 2010 show where FDA has gone beyond those defaults. Several cUTI programs met a 15-point margin[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=27)[220](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=220)[142](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=142)[655](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=655) . Recent CABP programs have generally used early clinical response at 72 to 120 hours in the ITT population, with margins as tight as 10 points[281](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=281)[284](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=284)[539](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=539) .


### Key takeaways


- **cUTI default:** composite clinical cure plus microbiological eradication in the micro-ITT population, assessed after the full treatment course plus at least 5 days of follow-up, with a 10% margin[59](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=59)[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=60) .
- **cUTI flexibility:** FDA's unmet-need guidance cites 15% as a potentially acceptable margin for patients with limited or no alternatives[80](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=80) . Vabomere, Zemdri, Fetroja and Zaynich were each approved on trials designed around a 15% margin[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=27)[220](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=220)[142](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=142)[655](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=655) .
- **CABP default:** improvement in CABP symptoms on day 4, with a 12.5% margin that rests on an M1 of at least 20 percentage points[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=70)[72](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=72)[73](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=73) .
- **CABP practice:** Xenleta, Nuzyra and Baxdela all report early clinical response (ECR) at 72 to 120 hours in all randomized (ITT) patients[281](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=281)[300](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=300)[649](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=649) . Xenleta's Trial 2 and the Nuzyra CABP trial reviewed prespecified a 10% margin[284](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=284)[539](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=539) .
- **Endpoint mismatch risk:** when a legacy trial used an older test-of-cure (TOC) endpoint, FDA re-analyzed it against an early-response endpoint. Teflaro and Zevtera are the examples[315](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=315)[597](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=597) .


### FDA guidance framework


#### cUTI: 2018 final guidance


FDA's final guidance *Complicated Urinary Tract Infections: Developing Drugs for Treatment* is dated June 1, 2018[42](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=42)[605](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=605) . Its core recommendations:


- **Primary endpoint:** a responder endpoint that combines microbiological success with clinical resolution in patients with microbiologically documented cUTI[59](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=59) .
- **Primary population:** micro-ITT, with consistency checked across the other analysis populations[59](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=59)[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=60) .
- **Timing:** a fixed time after randomization that covers the full course of antibacterial therapy plus at least 5 days of post-treatment observation. The NI margin is 10 percentage points[59](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=59) .
- **IV-to-oral switch designs:** FDA also supports the composite endpoint at about 5 days of IV therapy (the switch point), again with a 10-point margin. Patients should still be followed through the end of treatment and at least 5 days beyond, for example to about day 14 after randomization[61](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=61) .
- **Margin derivation (post-treatment endpoint):** FDA compared an upper bound of about 33% success without antibacterial therapy against a lower bound of about 70% from modern trials. That gives an estimated 37-point treatment effect, which FDA discounted to M1 = 30% before setting M2 = 10%[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=62)[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=63) .
- **Margin derivation (end-of-IV endpoint):** the comparison was 33% versus 56%, a 23-point effect discounted to M1 = 20%, with M2 = 10% chosen on clinical grounds[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=62)[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=63) .
- **Larger margins:** sponsors should discuss with FDA any proposed margin above 10%[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=62)[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=63) .


#### CABP: 2014 final guidance


FDA's final guidance *Community-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia: Developing Drugs for Treatment* is dated January 10, 2014[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=64)[604](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=604) .


- **Primary endpoint:** clinical response based on improvement in CABP symptoms (chest pain, cough frequency or severity, productive sputum, and difficulty breathing), assessed on day 4 after enrollment[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=70) .
- **Margin:** FDA considers 12.5 percentage points generally reasonable for the day-4 clinical-response endpoint. A larger margin may be considered in some circumstances, but sponsors should discuss it with FDA before the trial starts[72](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=72) .
- **Margin justification:** FDA judged an M1 of at least 20 percentage points to be a conservative estimate of the active-comparator effect on symptom improvement around days 3 to 5. That estimate supports an M2 of 12.5 points, and FDA notes that choosing M2 calls for clinical judgment and sponsor justification[73](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=73)[65](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=65) .
- **Analysis population:** the primary population should be agreed with FDA in advance. ITT (all randomized patients) is generally acceptable[699](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=699)[700](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=700) . For a narrow-spectrum drug, such as one active against a single genus and species, micro-ITT is the primary population[71](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=71) .
- **Secondary endpoints and follow-up:** secondary endpoints include day-4 response, clinical outcome at end of therapy, and symptom resolution at a fixed time after therapy[701](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=701) . The guidance calls for a post-therapy visit 5 to 10 days after treatment and an all-cause mortality assessment at day 28[702](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=702) . It also describes 28-day all-cause mortality as a possible primary endpoint, subject to feasibility and agreement with FDA[703](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=703) .


The 2024 ceftobiprole (Zevtera) review cites a 2020 FDA CABP guidance whose primary endpoint is day-4 improvement in at least two of chest pain, cough, productive sputum and difficulty breathing, with no worsening[601](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=601) .


#### Unmet-need and limited-population flexibility


- **Larger margins for limited-option populations:** under *Antibacterial Therapies for Patients With an Unmet Medical Need for the Treatment of Serious Bacterial Diseases* (2017), a margin larger than the disease-specific default may be acceptable for a drug intended for patients with limited treatment options. Acceptance depends on the type and degree of unmet need[78](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=78)[79](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=79)[607](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=607) .
- **cUTI example:** the guidance cites a margin above 10% but below the roughly 30% estimated treatment effect, such as 15%, as potentially acceptable[80](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=80) .
- **No CABP figure:** the retrieved guidance text gives no comparable CABP-specific figure[77](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=77) .
- **2025 Q&A:** the June 2025 Q&A guidance repeats that a randomized NI trial against best available therapy, supported by confirmatory evidence, can establish efficacy where unmet need remains[688](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=688)[613](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=613) .
- **LPAD pathway:** FDA describes NI trials with wider-than-traditional margins as one possible streamlined approach[81](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=81) .

#### Patterns in the cUTI record


**The 10% and 15% margins coexist.** The guidance default of 10% applies to Zerbaxa, Exblifep and Utebzi[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=22)[552](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=552)[660](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=660) . A 15% margin was prespecified and met for Vabomere, Zemdri, Fetroja and Zaynich[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=27)[220](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=220)[142](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=142)[655](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=655) . This matches the unmet-need guidance's example of 15% for cUTI[80](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=80) .


**Timing has moved toward fixed days after randomization.** Zerbaxa and Fetroja assessed TOC 7 ± 2 days after the last dose[261](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=261)[142](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=142) . Other programs fixed the visit relative to randomization or first dose:


- Day 17 ± 2 for Zemdri and Utebzi[220](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=220)[660](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=660)
- 19 (+2) days for Contepo[636](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=636)
- 21 to 25 days for Avycaz[237](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=237)


This is consistent with the guidance's recommendation of a fixed time point after randomization[59](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=59) .


**Early-timepoint endpoints for IV-only products.** Vabomere's primary endpoint was at end of IV therapy[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=27) . Avycaz and Zemdri paired a Day 5 endpoint with a later TOC endpoint[237](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=237)[220](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=220) . The Vabomere review notes that FDA guidance recommended both end of IV therapy and TOC as co-primary endpoints for IV-only drugs[209](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=209) . FDA's own Vabomere analysis also reported TOC results: 76.5% vs 73.2%, difference 3.3 (95% CI −6.2 to 13.0)[208](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=208) .


**Analysis-population choices can decide the outcome.**


- For Vabomere, FDA excluded two study sites over data-quality concerns. Its analysis population therefore differed from the applicant's, though noninferiority still held (difference 4.1, 95% CI 0.3 to 8.8)[208](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=208) .
- For tebipenem, FDA found that the earlier trial SPR994-301 did not meet its NI criterion when restricted to patients with ertapenem-susceptible pathogens. That finding led to a complete response letter and to the confirmatory SPR994-305 trial[661](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=661)[662](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=662) .
- In the Avycaz phase 2 review, FDA treated mMITT, not the applicant's ME population, as primary[244](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=244) .


**Microbiological thresholds vary.** Most programs defined eradication as reducing uropathogens to <10⁴ CFU/mL[261](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=261)[206](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=206)[142](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=142)[636](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=636) . Exblifep used <10³ CFU/mL[551](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=551) , and FDA's Recarbrio assessment also used <10³ CFU/mL[578](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=578) .


**A composite driven by microbiology.** In the Zaynich review, FDA observed that microbiological success largely drove the composite result. It considered noninferiority established but the interpretation of superiority uncertain[656](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=656) .

#### Patterns in the CABP record


**ECR at 72 to 120 hours in ITT is the operative primary endpoint.** Xenleta, Nuzyra and Baxdela define responders in similar terms[281](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=281)[300](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=300)[649](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=649) :


- the patient survived
- at least two of cough, sputum production, pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea improved
- none of those symptoms worsened
- no rescue antibacterial was given (Nuzyra also excludes discontinuation for an adverse event[301](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=301) )


In the Xenleta review, FDA kept the ITT ECR endpoint and added a worst-case analysis of indeterminate responses. Noninferiority held under both the applicant's and the worst-case analyses[282](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=282)[283](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=283)[288](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=288)[289](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=289) .


**Margins tighter than the guidance default.** The guidance supports 12.5%[72](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=72) . Xenleta's Trial 2 tightened its margin from 12.5% to 10% by protocol amendment[284](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=284) . The Nuzyra review records a prespecified 10% margin while noting the 12.5% guidance figure[539](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=539)[540](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=540) .


**Dual endpoints for FDA and EMA.** Xenleta's EMA-directed endpoint was investigator-assessed clinical response at TOC in a modified ITT population, with a 10% margin[284](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=284)[285](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=285) . Nuzyra reported investigator-assessed response at post-treatment evaluation as 87.6% vs 85.1%, difference 2.5 (95% CI −2.4 to 7.4)[541](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=541) . Baxdela reported investigator-assessed TOC success of 90.5% vs 89.7% (difference 0.8, 95% CI −3.3 to 4.8)[651](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=651)[652](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=652) .


**Legacy TOC trials were re-analyzed.**


- **Teflaro:** FDA did not accept the applicant's 10% margin for clinical cure at TOC because it lacked adequate historical justification. FDA instead analyzed Day 4 response in microbiologically confirmed patients against a 10-point margin, and both trials met it[315](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=315)[316](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=316)[103](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=103) .
- **Zevtera:** CAP-3001 was originally run with a TOC endpoint and a 15% margin, then re-analyzed for the US submission using Day 3 clinical success[596](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=596)[597](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=597) . The review notes that this Day 3 measure differs from the guidance's Day 4 symptom definition in timing and symptom scoring[601](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=601)[602](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=602) . The reviewer judged CAP-3001 adequate provided it was supported by positive findings in the program's SAB and ABSSSI indications[603](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=603) .


### Practical implications for development programs


1. **cUTI margin:** plan around 10% unless the target population has a documented unmet need. Programs that met 15% enrolled general cUTI populations, though Zemdri's and Fetroja's labels were limited to patients with limited or no alternative treatment options. FDA's guidance asks sponsors to discuss any margin above 10% in advance[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=62)[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=63)[80](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=80) .
2. **cUTI timing:** fix the TOC visit relative to randomization, and expect FDA to look closely at the micro-ITT population, including subsets defined by comparator susceptibility[59](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=59)[661](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=661) .
3. **IV-only products:** if a product has no oral step-down, an early (Day 5 or end of IV) endpoint paired with TOC fits both the guidance and recent precedent[61](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=61)[220](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=220)[209](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=209) .
4. **CABP endpoint and margin:** design around ECR at 72 to 120 hours in ITT. Recent precedent supports 10%, which is tighter than the 12.5% guidance figure, and an investigator-assessed TOC endpoint is often added for ex-US regulators[281](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=281)[284](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=284)[539](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=539)[285](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=285) .
5. **Legacy CABP trials:** if a trial used a TOC-only design, budget for an FDA re-analysis on an early-response endpoint. Retrospective endpoint definitions may not match the guidance exactly[315](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=315)[601](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=601)[602](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=602) .


### Open questions to explore further


The retrieved FDA records did not state the cUTI NI margins for Avycaz or Contepo, or the CABP margin for Baxdela[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=223)[637](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=637)[640](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=640) . Reviewing those approvals' statistical reviews directly would close the gaps. Other useful follow-ups:


- how FDA handled HABP/VABP all-cause mortality margins in the same programs
- how pediatric extrapolation from adult cUTI and CABP data has been accepted
- whether the 2020 CABP guidance version cited in the Zevtera review changed the 12.5% margin[601](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-noninferiority-margins?showSourceNumber=601)
